notes.decision: The transcription symbol ⳨ functions consistently as the letter ⲧ in this manuscript: ⲛ̄⳨ⲍⲉ = ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲉ 'thus' (glossary), ⲡⲓ⳨ⲟⲩ = ⲡⲓⲧⲟⲩ 'the five' (l.7), ⳨ⲛⲉⲩ = ⲧⲛⲉⲩ 'behold' (l.27). Rendered as ⲧ throughout.

Translated 'sweet' as antithesis to ⲉⲧⲥⲁϣⲉ 'bitter' in line 2 — the page's structuring gustatory-correspondential dyad (bitter trees vs. sweet fruits). The form is irregular; possible alternative readings include 'chosen' (ⲉⲧⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄) or a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉⲧϩⲗⲟϭ. Confidence moderate.

Preserved untranslated/transliterated; the form is obscure. Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ 'imprint/seal') with possessive nuance, or a verbal form. Glossed tentatively as 'he sealed.' Confidence low.

ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ is the Lycopolitan emphatic intensive 'himself' (cf. line 11 ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ 'himself'). The preceding ⲣⲁϩ is part of the lost word/phrase referring to the subject (likely the Father or his name); rendered 'himself' as completing the intensive construction.

Read as Lycopolitan plural of ⲛⲟⲩⲭ/ⲡⲟⲁⲗ 'lie, falsehood' = 'lies' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲟⲁⲗ 'the lie'). The line 'all the wickednesses are lies which came to be from him' echoes the polemical critique that the Errant doctrine treats wickedness as having divine origin.

Direct correspondential register: 'separating the Beautiful one (= the Light/God) forth from the Darkness' — capitalized as cosmic principle per terminology guide. Standard Manichaean cosmogonic act of separation.

ⲡⲙⲏⲧ here = ⲡⲙⲛⲧⲣⲉ 'the witness/testimony' rather than 'the midst.' The 'witness of the Judge of Truth' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲙⲏⲉ) is the standard Manichaean eschatological warrant. The chapter closes by appealing to this judicial witness as the guarantee that the disciples shall see at death what the Apostle has declared.

Untranslated word-fragment qualifying the presbyter; possibly the start of a Greek-derived adjective (ἐπάνω, ἐπανήκω) or a hapax title. Cf. line 25's lost word ending in -ⲙⲟⲥ which may be a parallel Greek loanword.
Compound ⲣⲉϥ-ϣⲙϣⲉ ('one who serves') + ⲉⲓⲇⲱⲗⲟⲛ (Greek εἴδωλον 'idol'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' The presbyter is a 'doer of idol-service' = pagan priest.

Distinguished from accumulated ⲡⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ 'people/community' (= δῆμος): here ⲡⲇⲟⲅⲙⲁ = Greek δόγμα 'doctrine, teaching' (already in glossary as ⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ). The chapter title and the presbyter's question both concern why this doctrine bears the name 'doctrine of Sin.'

Translated 'pluck/gather' from agricultural context (grape harvest, line 33 ⲛⲁⲭⲁⲗⲉϩ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲃⲱ ⲛ̄ⲉⲗⲁⲗⲉ 'shall pluck on the grape-vine'). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ϫⲱⲗⲕ̄/ⲕⲱⲗⲉϫ 'pluck, gather (fruit).' Reduplicated form ⲭⲉⲗⲗⲉϩ may be intensive.

Doubled discourse-marker 'in this manner; this manner also,' parallel to glossary entry ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲁⲛ 'in this same manner again.' Signals typological parallelism between the bitter-tree case and the grape-vine case in the presbyter's argument.
